clue.text: Take off wages — internal measure

indicators.note: internal says the measure sits inside the word for wages

parts.note: wages are pay
a rod is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a wage deduction that is measured internally.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them mockingly, which is a spoof or send-up.

clue.text: No more than nine, it appears, going to church -it can't be true!

parts.words: No more than nine, it appears
parts.note: a number no more than nine comes before ten, so read playfully as 'pre-ten'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A small congregation of nine or fewer heads to church amid disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase is a playful split: any number up to nine comes before ten, read as 'pre-ten'; 'going to' joins it to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham or false show is something that cannot be true.

clue.text: Unenterprising line of progress

parts.note: a dull, unvarying routine is like a groove worn in a road along which one plods without enterprise

explanation.definitionFit: A groove or routine one is stuck in is an unenterprising path forward.

clue.text: Is bossy and comes from Maidstone

indicators.note: the letters of the town come out in a fresh order, so the place's name is the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone from a Kent town is said to be domineering.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidstone is the county town of Kent in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bossy means ruling over and controlling others.

clue.text: The last good book on cryptic clues is worth digesting

indicators.note: the last of the word The supplies its final letter
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the following word is mixed up

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A reviewer recommends the latest fine book about cryptic clues as something worth reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the Good Book after the jumbled word clues (giving SCULE); 'is' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is fit to be eaten and digested.

clue.text: After this, Jack gets to the point

definitions.text: After this, Jack gets to the point

parts.words: After this, Jack gets to the point
parts.note: put Jack after the answer and you have a workman who climbs church spires, reaching their pointed tips

explanation.definitionFit: A church spire rises to a point, and a steeplejack climbs it.

clue.text: Cats are, when the doctor leaves

definitions.text: Cats are, when the doctor leaves

indicators.note: leaves says the doctor goes out of the word for what cats are

parts.note: cats are mousers, catchers of mice
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Pets seem to take advantage once the vet has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats are MOUSERS; when MO (the doctor) leaves, the rest remains, and the whole clue hints that the cats exploit the absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who exploit others are takers, like pets taking advantage.

clue.text: Nice cream bun I dropped —— confounded nuisance!

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letter I is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone drops a cream bun and curses the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' tells you to remove I from NICE CREAM BUN before 'confounded' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or hindrance is a troublesome thing that gets in the way.

clue.text: In explosive situation, have a drink. It's a gift

indicators.note: In places the drink inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is a high explosive
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: In a tense moment someone pauses for a drink, a natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is often called a gift.

clue.text: So pure? He isn't really!

indicators.note: not really so pure suggests those letters are not what they seem and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who looks so virtuous is really a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: An affected person putting on airs only pretends to qualities.

clue.text: Old-time engineers unprepared

parts.note: EX means former or old
tempo is musical time
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned engineers are caught unready.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff is done without preparation.

clue.text: Do well with fish, getting about ninety

indicators.note: getting about means the fish wraps around the number

parts.note: an eel is a fish
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An angler does well by catching a fish weighing about ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine or be outstanding is to do well.

clue.text: Old play on words for example, is back. Cut it out!

parts.note: EX means former or old
a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: is back means the abbreviation for 'for example' is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone tired of an old pun told again demands that it stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete or strike out is to remove a passage.

clue.text: Cut tropical harvest — using money for power-tool

indicators.note: harvest stirs up the gathered letters of the crop words

explanation.surface: A tropical crop is cut by a wealthy grower using power tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by the wealthy is government where riches buy power.

clue.text: No stamp? Turn to him

indicators.note: turn shuffles the letters of the two opening words

explanation.surface: Someone without a stamp asks the person on the round for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier is the person who handles letters and stamps.

clue.text: Employed when selling a length, in order to stop short, cuts?

definitions.text: in order to stop short, cuts?

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper measures off a length while taking steps to cut losses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop counter has a ruler fixed for measuring cloth sold by length; also a step taken to check a threat, such as spending cuts.

clue.text: Perhaps is repairing road, with irritation

parts.note: ST is street, a road
itching is skin irritation

explanation.surface: Road works cause irritation for passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing up a tear is one way of mending, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: .Shut in small room, many stole out, newsman found

parts.note: C is a hundred, many

indicators.note: out means the word stole is put out of order

parts.note: ED is an editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: A reporter finds many people slipping out of a small room with stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept private in a cupboard-like room means secluded.

clue.text: Walk within the law

explanation.surface: A stroll that stays legal.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk walk for health is a stroll; and lawful under a state's founding charter.

clue.text: One spin doctor I had found lacking taste

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: doctor means tamper with, so the letters of spin are altered

parts.note: I'd contracts I had

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor's offering was bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland, flavourless food lacks taste.

clue.text: Is nude, having cast them off?

definitions.text: Is nude, having cast them off?

indicators.note: cast means throw about, so the letters of the two words are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone is naked after throwing off their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is what a naked person has removed.

clue.text: Muslim leader has a cheek, going into church

indicators.note: going into says the cheek goes inside the church

parts.note: lip means cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: An impudent religious leader enters a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor to Muhammad as ruler of the Islamic world.

clue.text: Sails about to flap? There's not a breath of wind

definitions.text: There's not a breath of wind

indicators.note: flap means move loosely, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Sails hang limp as the wind dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Still weather with no breeze is stuffy and calm.

clue.text: Always poetic? That is weird

parts.note: e'er is the poetic form of ever, always
IE abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A strange poem keeps repeating the word always.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny and strange things are spooky.

clue.text: Cutting short their harbour operations?

parts.note: to dock is to cut short a tail, and port workers handle vessels at the quay

explanation.definitionFit: Port labourers work at docks loading and unloading ships.

clue.text: Heading the mission that's promoting cessation

definitions.text: Heading the mission that's promoting cessation

parts.words: Heading the mission that's promoting cessation
parts.note: placed at the head of the word mission, this makes a break or pause in a show

explanation.definitionFit: Put in front of 'mission', it forms a word for an interval or pause in proceedings.

clue.text: Put forward, I'd secured top job

indicators.note: secured means the contraction is held inside

parts.note: present means put forward
taken as I and D, the contraction I'd

explanation.surface: Someone proposed for promotion claims the top position.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a country or company holds the top role; the officeholder stands for the post.

clue.text: First mate appears, as always, right away

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: The first officer appears promptly, as always.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the first woman and partner of Adam.

clue.text: Leaving hospital can die, abandoned, at a home overseas

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A patient discharged from hospital fears dying, left alone abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' is read as 'setting off first', so H leads, then the jumble of CAN DIE (ACIEND) and A; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large estate house in Spanish-speaking lands.

clue.text: Of one mind about the old folk going out

indicators.note: going out means the old folk surround the word for about

parts.note: the aged are old people
RE means about

explanation.surface: Elderly people agree to go out together.
explanation.definitionFit: People in accord share the same view.
